item.title: Carrick expects Man Utd stay despite Chelsea defeat
item.description: Michael Carrick's Manchester United are winless in nine games (Glyn KIRK) Michael Carrick said he expects to remain in charge of Manchester United for Tuesday's Champions League visit of Roma despite a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea that stretched the club's winless run to nine matches. Carrick was given a stay of execution by the United hierarchy after a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth last weekend when many expected the axe to fall on the former England midfielder. United were much improved during the first half at Stamford Bridge but paid for a lack of ruthlessness as the visitors wasted a number of chances to take the lead. Morgan Rogers strolled through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring early in the second half. Lisandro Martinez was then shown two quick yellow cards and conceded a penalty, converted by Cole Palmer, to kill off any hope of a United fightback. "Yes," Carrick told TNT Sports when asked if he expected to remain in charge for the Roma match. "We've got to move forward. We've got to take the things that we felt worked for us today and take a bit of belief and the confidence from that and a lot of the good things, especially in the first half." United's longest winless run for 38 years leaves them just one point above the Premier League relegation zone and at risk of dropping into the bottom three by the end of the weekend. "From being in such a good place in the first half, the two halves of football couldn't probably be more further apart in some ways," added Carrick. "I think the way they went about it and played, the quality of football and the way we played in the first half, definitely gives encouragement. We've got to take that." Two defeats in their first three Champions League games have left United 20th in the 36-team table and at risk of missing out on the knockout stages. kca/mw

item.title: Blue Jays predicted to sign $6.1M ex-Braves World Series champion, 2-time Gold Glove winner
item.description: Blue Jays predicted to sign $6.1M ex-Braves World Series champion, 2-time Gold Glove winner originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays were just a couple of outs away from winning the World Series a year ago, but Miguel Rojas of the Los Angeles Dodgers had other plans. The disappointment carried over into 2026, as Toronto failed to even make the playoffs. A big reason for that was the number of injuries the team dealt with throughout the season, making it difficult to find any consistency. The Blue Jays will be looking to add players who can stay healthy this winter. “Some injuries, you can see coming. When the 42-year-old Max Scherzer runs into a few IL stints, no one should be surprised. When José Berríos has Tommy John surgery after not missing a start for nearly a decade, it's terribly unfortunate, but we all understand the realities of baseball and the limitations of the human elbow. The Blue Jays are trying to find that line now between bad luck and controllable variables," MLB.com's Keegan Matheson wrote. While pitching will certainly be an area Toronto looks to improve, the infield could also use some attention. “The infield largely remains the same. Toronto hopes for a bounce-back season from Guerrero Jr., while Clement and Gimenez are up the middle, and Okamoto stays at the hot corner. The Blue Jays could add another low-cost infielder this offseason,” SI’s Zion Trammell wrote. CBS Sports' Mike Axisa believes that super-utility man Mauricio Dubón could be a great addition for Toronto. “Every contender could use a player like Dubón. He's a true super utility guy who can play every position except catcher -- and play it well. Offensively, Dubón is an aggressive bat-to-ball player with a knack for ideal launch angles, which, in English, means he's a line drive hitter. He obliterated his previous career high in games played and plate appearances this past season and handled the workload well,” Axisa wrote. For the Blue Jays, adding Dubón would be a great move, especially considering he is coming off the best season of his career in several different ways. Toronto would be getting a versatile player who could fill multiple roles, but the challenge will be prying him away from Atlanta. Dubón was on a $6.1 million contract with the Braves. There would be plenty of opportunities for him on Toronto's roster, but the strong support he has received from his teammates in Atlanta could ultimately convince him to stay. item.title: Staff score predictions for Clemson’s massive road matchup vs Florida State
item.description: Clemson and Florida State have both fallen well short of expectations this season, but Saturday night’s matchup in Tallahassee still carries plenty of intrigue as the longtime ACC rivals look to get things back on track. The Tigers (4-3, 2-2 ACC) are hitting the road for the first time in more than a month, looking to bounce back from a frustrating 20-16 loss to Virginia Tech. Clemson appeared to be in position to secure another conference victory before the Hokies scored the go-ahead touchdown in the final two minutes. True freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds continues to gain valuable experience, but Clemson’s offense has struggled to find consistency. Reynolds completed 20 of 26 passes for 153 yards against Virginia Tech, although four sacks made things difficult for the young signal-caller. Florida State (3-4, 1-3 ACC) enters the matchup coming off a bye week, giving the Seminoles extra time to prepare. Before the break, FSU pushed No. 1 Miami to double overtime in a 43-35 loss, with quarterback Ashton Daniels accounting for five touchdowns. Recent history favors Clemson, which has won nine of its last 10 meetings with Florida State. However, with both programs searching for answers, neither team can afford to take anything for granted. Saturday’s contest kicks off at 7 p.m. ET at Doak Campbell Stadium, with ACC Network carrying the broadcast. Can Clemson continue its recent success against the Seminoles, or will Florida State defend its home field? Here’s how our staff sees Saturday night’s matchup playing out. Alex Turri: Clemson 17, Florida State 21 While Florida State’s defense has been one of the worst in college football this season, Clemson’s offense is doing the same thing. For me, this game comes down to which unit can step up and played just a little better than their norm. Unfortunately, I think the Seminoles’ defense is more likely to rise to the occasion. You need to be able to throw the ball in college football to truly succeed, and Clemson just can’t do it. Road loss for Dabo Swinney and the Tigers. Steve Holley: Clemson 19, Florida State 23 Clemson's offense hasn't been able to find the end zone more than once in either of its last two ACC games. Florida State has given up plenty of yards -- 434.9 per game this season, which ranks eighth from last in all of FBS. It's hard for me at this point to trust this Clemson offense for long drives that end in six points. Expect a close and competitive game like most Clemson-FSU matchups, but simply put: I trust FSU's bottom-of-the-barrel defense more than Clemson's bottom-of-the-barrel offense. item.title: Scotland's women lose Euro curling semi before men eye final spot
item.description: Scotland's women are next up against Lithuania on Friday afternoon [Getty Images] Scotland's women will play for bronze at the European Curling Championships on Sunday after narrowly losing a tense semi-final against Switzerland. Fay Henderson's rink had secured their place in the last four with a game to spare, but could not overcome former world champion Alina Paetz's rink, who remain unbeaten in the event in the Czech Republic. The Scots had eked out a 3-1 lead after five ends, but the Swiss scored one in each of the final three ends to earn a place in the final against Sweden. Henderson and her team will now play Latvia in Ostrava on Sunday (xx GMT), with the skip looking to add the the silver and bronze she claimed as an alternate in the past two championships. Later on Saturday, Scotland's men will face unbeaten Sweden in the semi-finals - live on the BBC iPlayer and BBC Sport website and app - after losing their 100% record thanks to a disappointing 6-5 defeat by Italy. That meant Grant Hardie's rink finished second in their group behind Stefano Spiller's side, who face the Czechs in the other semi-final. Against Italy, the Scots were always playing catch-up after losing two in the opening end. Hardie's rink did manage to edge ahead at 4-3 after the sixth, but the Italians took two in the seventh and, although the Scots then levelled to take the match into an extra-end, lead Ross Whyte was short with his final stone to concede defeat. item.title: Ocon unexpectedly replaced at Haas for the rest of Mexican GP weekend
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Haas driver Esteban Ocon arriving at the Monza circuit, ahead of FP3 and qualifying. (is associated with: «Ocon unexpectedly replaced at Haas for the rest of Mexican GP weekend») David Davies/PA Wire/dpa Esteban Ocon was replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the rest of the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix weekend in an unexpected move by his Haas team. The announcement came in a statement on Saturday, ahead of third practice and qualifying later. Ryo had already participated in first practice on Friday. "The Japanese driver will partner teammate Ollie Bearman through final practice and qualifying on Saturday and Sunday's 71-lap grand prix - marking Ryo's Formula 1 race debut," Haas said. The team didn't explain the reason why Ocon was being replaced and said "no further statements will be made at this time." According to media reports, Ocon isn't injured nor ill. The driver initially did not make any comment. Ocon's contract with Haas is valid until the end of the season. The team had already announced that Brazilian Rafael Camara will drive alongside Bearman next year.

item.title: Real Madrid make firm decision on January exit for 28-year-old defender – report
item.description: Real Madrid make firm decision on January exit for 28-year-old defender – report Real Madrid have performed very well in recent weeks, winning five games on the bounce and playing much better football under Jose Mourinho. The Portuguese manager’s tactical tweaks have worked wonders for the team but have come at a cost for players like Trent Alexander-Arnold. The Englishman has now fallen behind both captain Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries in the right-back hierarchy. However, according to journalist Jorge Picon (h/t Defensa Central ), Real Madrid have no intention of selling Trent during the January transfer window. Despite his limited game time, the club do not want to part ways with Trent, and the former Liverpool star also wants to stay and fight for his place. Real Madrid rule out January departure for Trent Trent has not had a great time in the Spanish capital since joining from the Merseyside club at the start of last season. Mourinho’s arrival has done little to change the situation, with the manager initially preferring to start Dumfries ahead of him. Valverde has emerged as Real Madrid’s first choice right-back. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) In recent weeks, Valverde has emerged as Mourinho’s first-choice right-back, which has given the team more defensive solidity. Trent has started just four of Real Madrid’s opening 13 matches this season, but Mourinho has confirmed that both he and Dumfries will get minutes. The Portuguese manager revealed at the press conference ahead of the Racing Santander game that one of the duo will start tomorrow. However, the 28-year-old did not come to Spain from England to be the third-choice right-back, and talk has already intensified about a potential return to Liverpool. Nevertheless, Picon has confirmed that Real Madrid are unwilling to sanction a winter departure, and his situation will only be reconsidered in the summer of 2027. Trent determined to win Mourinho’s trust For his part, Trent is keen to convince Mourinho that he deserves an extended run as the starting right-back. Can Trent work his way back into Jose Mourinho’s plans? (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) His passing range, crossing ability and creativity remain underutilised aspects of his game, but he needs to show more commitment defensively. Mourinho would do well to use Trent in La Liga games where opponents sit in a deep block, as the Englishman is capable of unlocking their defences for Los Blancos . Keeping him until at least the summer is a sensible decision. Selling him mid-season does not benefit Real Madrid and only takes an option away from them. It also gives Trent the opportunity to let his performances do the talking and save his faltering Los Blancos career. All eyes will now be on whether the Englishman starts against Racing Santander tomorrow and how he fares in the coming weeks if given the opportunity.

item.description: Michigan Football returns to action Saturday afternoon, traveling to Piscataway for a Halloween matchup against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights. With both teams struggling to find consistency this season, the Wolverines will look to reel things in and build some much-needed momentum heading into November. Michigan enters Saturday’s contest with a 4-3 record (1-3 Big Ten) after suffering a frustrating 13-6 loss to Indiana last weekend. item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves are set to decline their option on Cody Williams. The 6’8″ wing joined the Wolves after two years with the Utah Jazz, but he has failed to break into the team. His performances have been far below those of other rotation players. At that point, as things stand, the 21-year-old is set to become an unrestricted free agent as the Wolves have decided against triggering their fourth-year team option. item.title: 5 Things I Think I Think About the Miami Dolphins After Week 7
item.description: Wait, what? Did the Miami Dolphins respond to arguably their worst loss of the season with their first win? On the road? You bet your sweet bippy they did. And against the Jets too – if you tell me the Dolphins go 2-15 this season but sweep the Jets, I’d say, “You know, not so bad.” Here are five more things I think I think following the Dolphins’ first win. They Did the One Thing Winning Teams Do If there’s one ultimate flex in professional football, it’s this: Running the ball to drain the clock and close out a close game. Everybody in the stadium knows exactly what’s coming: The defense knows, the crowd knows, the broadcast team knows, everybody knows. And it doesn’t matter – the winning team lines up and closes the game anyway. On Sunday, that’s unexpectedly what the Dolphins were able to do against the Jets. Late in the fourth quarter, the Jets scored a touchdown (Mason Taylor?! Again?!) to pull within three points. They then kicked off, hoping to force a stop and get the ball back to tie or win it. The old Dolphins would have played conservative, forcing the Jets to burn their timeouts but giving Gang Green the ball and a chance to win. But what did the new Dolphins do? 3:17 left, 1 st down, 14-yard run from Ollie Gordon. Jets timeout. 3:10 left, 1 st down, 7-yard run from Ollie Gordon. Jets timeout. 3:04 left, 2 nd down, 1-yard run from Ollie Gordon. 2:21 left, 3 rd down, 1-yard run from Ollie Gordon. Two-minute warning. 2:00 left, 4 th down, 2-yard run from Malik Willis. First down. Victory formation. I mean, it wasn’t pure dominance: They needed a two-yard pickup on fourth down to secure the win, whereas ideally you’d lock that in on second or third down. Still, if you want to talk about the growth of a young team, this is Exhibit A with a gold star. Malik Willis Showed Tangible Growth What a difference a bye week makes, eh? Let’s revel in the stat line: 14-of-21 passing 228 passing yards 2 passing touchdowns 0 interceptions, 0 fumbles 37 rushing yards 1 rushing touchdown QB rating of 130.7! So what caused the change? A good night’s sleep? Frank Thomas’ testosterone supplements?* Yes and yes. But also, maybe better decision-making and resource utilization. Instead of going for deep shot after deep shot, against the Jets Willis threw more passes that were short of the sticks, completing a season-high 67% of his passes and keeping the offense on schedule. He also involved his tight ends more, with TE Greg Dulcich leading the team in targets and a season-high 86 yards, and he clearly benefited from having No. 1 receiver Caleb Douglas back. Willis still has more questions than answers right now, of course. item.title: 100% dribbles, 4 shots: Amad stands tall amid the wreckage as Man United lose to Chelsea
item.description: 100% dribbles, 4 shots: Amad stands tall amid the wreckage as Man United lose to Chelsea Manchester United forward Amad provided a rare positive as he and his teammates slipped to another defeat, this time against Chelsea. Beaten United’s woeful run continued as they were beaten 2-0 by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. The Red Devils produced a promising first-half performance, creating chances and dominating possession, but they were unable to make it count. Chelsea emerged for the second half with greater intensity and took control of the match. The deadlock was broken in the 50th minute by Morgan Rogers, who was allowed to dance into the box and fire beyond Senne Lammens. Chelsea doubled their lead 15 minutes later through Cole Palmer, who beat Lammens from the penalty spot. The hosts were awarded a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was judged to have fouled Wesley Fofana inside the box while United were defending a corner. Replays showed that Martinez did not even look at the ball and was firmly fixated on Fofana. The World Cup winner was shown a second yellow card and consequently sent off, leaving United with a mountain to climb. United sit in 17th place in the Premier League table and could slip into the bottom three by the end of the matchweek. Amad’s display Several United players were awful , but one who can hold his head high is Amad. The Ivorian was United’s primary source of threat, especially in the first half. He fired four shots, two of which were on target. Amad really should have been on the scoresheet. Presented with a golden chance after pinching the ball off Fofana, he blazed it over the bar. The United star found his teammates with 19 of the 22 passes he attempted (86.4% individual pass accuracy). He also embarked on two dribbles, completing both of them. item.description: Thierno Barry scored Everton's third goal in their Carabao Cup fourth round match [Press Association] Everton striker Thierno Barry has said he was relieved that his family were not at home when it was burgled while he played in a cup match. His home in Greater Manchester was targeted while he was playing for Everton against Newcastle United in a Carabao Cup tie at the Hill Dickinson stadium on Thursday. "The most important thing in life is to look after and protect the people you love. "That's what truly matters. Everything else is just materialistic." item.title: Pogacar 'happy to be alive' after 'scary' crash
item.description: Tadej Pogacar has won six Grand Tour titles [Getty Images] Five-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogacar says he is "just happy to be alive", two months after suffering three fractured vertebrae in a crash. The 28-year-old Slovenian was ruled out for the season after crashing during the Vuelta a Espana in August . Pogacar required surgery on a broken collarbone and was initially diagnosed with a fracture in his neck, but further scans in his home country revealed more injuries. "I knew I had a C7 fracture, but then we saw I had two more broken vertebrae, the T1 and T2," Pogacar told The Athletic . "At that moment, I was happy I didn't do the European Championships, which had been my initial goal. When I saw I had three broken vertebrae? I'm just happy to be alive actually, or just to be standing." Pogacar also suffered concussion during the crash, which left him struggling with dizziness, nausea and poor co-ordination in the weeks afterwards. He said the extent of the concussion meant he was unable to shower by himself. "I had to be showered with the help of the team doctor. I could not shower. I was getting dizzy as soon as I stood or when I put my head down," Pogacar added. "I was just completely out of it and it was so tough." When he came off his bike, Pogacar was aiming to complete the set of Grand Tour titles by adding the Vuelta to his single Giro d'Italia victory and five Tour de France wins. His injuries meant he was unable to defend his rainbow jersey at the World Championships in Montreal last month. Pogacar said the first few weeks of recovery were difficult and he was "mentally not OK" and "not a fun person to be around". He said his mood improved once he resumed rehabilitation and indoor training. "When I started to get on the home trainer, to go to physio every day, then I started to feel better, also in the head. But it was a day-to-day fight," he said. "I don't have discomfort any more. I have to be careful not to crash on the bike, or do some heavy lifting with my left arm or with my neck. But I can do basically everything normal now." Pogacar's team UAE Team Emirates-XRG said the decision not to race again until 2027 would allow him to return to full health "without placing a timeline on his return to competition". Pogacar is aiming to return next year, but will do so with a more cautious mindset. "If I crash again on the bike now, it can be very problematic. Everybody says that I was lucky, and you're always lucky after a crash where you can walk away and you're fine," said Pogacar. "You see it's pretty serious and not to joke around. It's a bit scary, to be honest, to think about it."

The first Saturday in May might be a ways away, but as has been established, it is never too early to start dreaming about Kentucky Derby weekend. Unbeaten Emphatic Out Front In Kentucky Oaks Race In this, her biggest test to date, Emphatic again put her best hoof forward in the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies at Keeneland. Running with authority, this two-year-old daughter of Nyquist firmly placed herself atop the list of Kentucky Oaks contenders by picking up her fourth win in as many career starts. Breaking smoothly from post 10 and stalking a hot early pace set by Lexi’s Charm (22.54 opening quarter, 45.87 half mile), the spirited filly took the lead ¾ of mile into the race and never looked back. A huge turn of foot at the top of the stretch placed Emphatic four lengths ahead of her eleven rivals and she held off a late charge from Miss Monica to clear the wire a length and a half to the good. Completing the mile and a sixteenth in 1:44.23, this marked the second consecutive grade 1 win for Emphatic as she had been brilliant in gate-to-wire fashion while winning the Darley Alcibades Stakes at Keeneland on October 2. Emphatic (10) ridden by Tyler Gaffalione wins the Breeders Cup Juvenile Fillies (Grade 1) on Future Stars Friday at the Breeders' Cup World Championships at Keeneland Race Course in Lexington, Kentucky on October 30, 2026. item.description: Why Colts are playing Jonathan Taylor in Week 8 despite trade rumors heating up originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jonathan Taylor trade rumors are picking up a lot of steam heading into the Indianapolis Colts ' Week 8 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars . Saturday morning revealed that the Colts are seemingly more open to a trade with Taylor than before, and it looks like a trade is very much on the table for Indianapolis. So, with the odds of a deal increasing, will Taylor even play in Week 8? According to ESPN's Stephen Holder , Taylor is still set to play for the Colts on Sunday. So, with that in mind, why are the Colts, despite the trade rumors picking up a lot of steam lately, not benching Taylor? Why Jonathan Taylor is still set to play for Colts despite trade rumors heating up "As of now, Jonathan Taylor IS playing tomorrow," Holder reports. "No deal is imminent, and I imagine they want to send the message that they are willing to keep him (which I do believe is true)." So, while conventional wisdom might suggest that the Colts should bench Taylor and protect him from getting hurt and ruining his trade value, the Colts still plan to play the star running back on Sunday. One of the reasons, as Holder notes, is to prove to other teams around the NFL that they're willing to keep Taylor. Benching him would prove that they fully intend to trade him away. The Colts wouldn't bench a star player like Taylor if a trade weren't already completed or agreed upon. If Taylor doesn't play, the Colts tip their hand and would effectively ruin the leverage they have in trade talks. MORE : NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts ’ Jonathan Taylor Benching Taylor without having a trade in place would be a mistake. Besides, there's still a decent chance Taylor won't be traded, even as these rumors heat up Saturday morning. If they benched him but ended up keeping him, their decision to sit him in Week 8 would look a lot stranger than if they play him in Week 8 and then trade him the following week. At the end of the day, the Colts are planning to play Taylor in Week 8 against the AFC South rival Jaguars, despite trade rumors picking up a lot of steam about the star RB. They are running the risk of injury with Taylor, but they can limit his reps in this game to preserve his health, while still giving him a chance to see the field for what could be the final time with the Colts. This Colts team is selling, as they've already shipped out Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and Josh Downs has requested a trade. Taylor might be on the move, and that could still be the case even if he plays on Sunday. item.title: Kane beat Mbappe to Ballon d'Or by just 28 points
item.description: Harry Kane beat second-placed Kylian Mbappe to the men's Ballon d'Or by just 28 points - one of the smallest winning margins in the award's history. Organisers released voting numbers on Saturday, showing that England captain Kane was awarded 1,055 points, compared with 1,027 for Real Madrid's France forward Mbappe. Bayern Munich striker Kane became the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, while France talisman Mbappe also claimed his best finish, ending up well clear of Spain forward Lamine Yamal, who was third with 881 points. It was the smallest winning margin since Argentina great Lionel Messi beat Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk by seven points in 2019, while the men's Ballon d'Or has twice been decided by a single point. That happened when England World Cup winner Bobby Charlton, who was later knighted, beat Portugal star Eusebio by the smallest possible margin in 1966, and Germany defender Matthias Sammer repeated the tight one-point victory when he edged out Brazil striker Ronaldo in 1996. Mbappe may take heart from Ronaldo's Ballon d'Or experience as the legendary frontman, who presented Kane with his award in London on Monday, went on to win in 1997 and again in 2002. Harry Kane is the fifth English player to win the Ballon d'Or, after Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966), Kevin Keegan (1978 & 1979) and Michael Owen (2001) [Getty Images] Kane clinched the prize after scoring 73 goals in 65 matches last season, helping Bayern Munich to a league and cup double and leading England to a third-place finish at the World Cup. The award is decided by votes from 100 journalists, using a weighted points system. Top 10 in the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or: Harry Kane - 1,055 points Kylian Mbappe - 1,027 points Lamine Yamal - 881 points Rodri - 726 points Lionel Messi - 612 points Khvicha Kvaratskhelia - 541 points Ousmane Dembele - 418 points Erling Haaland - 378 points Michael Olise - 296 points Fabian Ruiz - 201 points Ranking England's Ballon d'Or winners - how does Kane compare?
